title: Certificate relates to the melt: how the cutting calculation reveals the gap down to specific parts
description: From a 6000 mm bar, eight 700 mm blanks were taken out by record, with 24 mm losses and a 1000 mm remainder. We examine the extra 624 mm, the primary records, and the completed correction of the remainder.
seo_title: Certificate of melt and parts: material consumption calculation
seo_description: 6000 mm, 8 × 700, losses 24 and remainder 1000: why the balance is exceeded by 624 mm. Request and correction based on primary data without substituting the origin.
seo_keywords: melt certificate and parts, blank cutting balance, material traceability nuclear plant, bar remainder error
content:
A material certificate confirms the relevant properties of the material, but does not automatically explain the origin of a specific part. In addition to identifiers, it is useful to check the consistency of blank consumption. If more material was recorded as obtained from a single bar than it contained, a copy of the certificate does not close the gap. Below is a calculation example where the error is found in the remainder statement, and its correction requires primary records, not a convenient figure.

One bar and eight blanks

Conditional certificate C-81 relates to melt material P-81. In the chain under consideration, bar B-7 with a length of 6000 mm was received. From it, according to the cutting record, eight 700 mm blanks were made for parts D-1 through D-8. The total length losses, separately specified in the same given record, amounted to 24 mm. In the warehouse statement, the remainder of B-7 is recorded as 1000 mm.

All lengths in the training calculation are assumed to relate to a single bar and a single accounting basis; their accuracy and possible tolerances are not investigated here. This is a check of the internal arithmetic consistency of the submitted data, not an assignment of cutting technology or production allowance.

First, let us add up the eight blanks: 8 × 700 = 5600 mm. With the specified losses, the consumption amounted to 5624 mm. The expected remainder from these data is 6000 − 5624 = 376 mm. Together with the recorded remainder of 1000 mm, this gives 6624 mm — 624 mm more than the original length. The same stated history cannot be true in all its parts.

What the calculation established and what it did not

A contradiction in the consumption chain of B-7 is established. It is not established that melt P-81 is counterfeit, that all parts were made from different material, or that the certificate itself is wrong. Possible causes: an error in the remainder, a different actual source of some blanks, an incorrect number of parts, or a wrong link in the record. The cause must not be chosen by the lowest cost of correction. If different forms state the length before processing and the size of the finished part, first bring the accounting items to a comparable basis without mixing them.

Also, one cannot simply write 376 mm into the warehouse document based on this article. This is a mathematically consistent value, but not yet a proven actual remainder. If some blanks came from a different bar, correcting one figure will only hide another origin chain.

Completed request on the gap

For B-7, the following are recorded: original 6000 mm, eight 700 mm blanks, losses of 24 mm, and a remainder of 1000 mm. The sum is 6624 mm and exceeds the original length by 624 mm. We ask to reconcile the primary cutting record, the belonging of D-1 through D-8, and the actual remainder; to establish the source of the discrepancy. The value 376 mm is the calculated remainder under the stated premises and is not considered an independent confirmation of the fact. We ask to preserve the link of the proper correction to the original record.

Such a request immediately sets a verifiable discrepancy. It is more useful than a general request to "provide traceability," which usually results in C-81 being sent again. The certificate may be correct, but it answers a different question. What is needed are data connecting B-7 to the actually manufactured blanks.

Completed conditional outcome: remainder transferred in error

Suppose the primary cutting record and the provided remainder reconciliation confirm 376 mm, and the statement compiler established a transfer of 1000 mm from an adjacent line of a different material. The belonging of D-1 through D-8 to B-7 is confirmed by the relevant production records. Then the correction relates to the warehouse statement: the established basis and the history of the correction are preserved, without retroactively changing C-81.

After the correction, the arithmetic is consistent: 5600 + 24 + 376 = 6000 mm. In our outcome, there is also the primary link of the parts to B-7, so the calculation supports rather than substitutes it. One equality without these records would not prove the origin. One can devise an arithmetically neat table for any material; verifiable history is created by actual data.

If primary data show two bars

Then the original statement "eight blanks from B-7" is changed according to the fact. It is established which parts relate to the second bar and what its material document is. There is no need to artificially force everything to reconcile in one line. Even two bars of the same melt must have sufficient linkage to the relevant operations if it is required by the accepted procedure.

For nuclear products, applicable requirements are determined by the subject and stage; NP-071-26 will enter into force on December 19, 2026, as of October 28 this is a future date. If the certificate exists but material consumption does not reconcile, you can contact NPI "Nedra" with one contradictory chain and the primary record of its formation.
